requirement:
Plain text defines no attachments. The file root and each `line` item have
empty attachment lists, including lines that begin with comment delimiters
from another language.
rationale:
**Obligations.** `requirements.sdk.sources.plain-text.attachments` says that:
- the plain-text file root has an empty attachment list;
- each `line` item has an empty attachment list;
- this holds even for lines that begin with comment delimiters from another language.

**Test.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` carries `{test}` for this requirement. Its `test.txt` case parses `"# just text\n"` through `OutlineContent::from_source`. It then collects the attachments of every item with `outline().items.iter().flat_map(|i| &i.attachments)` and asserts the result equals `vec![]`.

**Coverage.**
- **Root and line items:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` shows that the outline items for plain text are the root plus one item per non-blank line. The flat-map over all items therefore covers both the root and the `line` item.
- **Foreign comment delimiter:** the line starts with `#`, a comment delimiter of Python, YAML and TOML. In those languages the same loop does produce `Comment` attachments, for example `# standalone` in the YAML case, so the plain-text expectation is a real contrast.
- **Assertion:** `assert_eq!` against an empty vector would fail if the root or the line gained any attachment.

**Residual risk.** Only `#` is exercised as the foreign delimiter. `//`, `/* */`, `<!-- -->` and `@decorator` are not tried on plain text. The requirement states a single rule, "empty lists, including lines that begin with comment delimiters from another language." The test covers that class with one representative. I confirmed with `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/mod.rs#fn[plain_text]` that no per-language branching is involved, since the plain-text implementation does no comment or annotation classification of its own. I treat the extra delimiters as further values of an already represented input class, not as a gap.

No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.
